consensus_summary: The Sabbath primarily symbolizes God's creational rest fulfilled as spiritual rest in Christ and the remaining eschatological rest for the people of God.
book_summary: The Sabbath is the complete seven—the six-and-one unit counted by the law at every scale (week, land year, jubilee of seven sevens)—with the rest-day as crown of the whole that the word itself sometimes names.
consensus_core_identification: spiritual/eschatological rest in God and Christ
book_core_identification: complete seven (six-and-one structural unit whose seventh is rest)
boundary_disagreement: None applicable; the book does not operate inside the consensus rest-centric frame, so questions of which rest cases are included or excluded do not arise.
material_contradiction: None; the book neither denies rest nor replaces a shared referent, but supplies an identification absent from the consensus primary and alternatives.
rationale: Consensus cores (and listed alternatives) uniformly center rest—creational, soteriological in Christ, eschatological—with secondary layers of covenant sign, day-observance transfer, liberation, or millennial week. The book's minimum core is instead the heptadic unit itself (six-plus-one at multiple legal scales, rest as crown, week called sabbath). That structural-completeness identification is not covered by the consensus primary or any alternative, yielding novelty rather than refinement or contradiction.
strongest_objection: The dominant Christian tradition, controlled by Hebrews 3–4 and Colossians 2, treats rest in Christ as the settled symbolic core; a purely structural heptad reading leaves that controlling typology unengaged.
